title: One brooch is carved from a meteorite strike.
description:
One brooch is carved from a meteorite strike. The scarab at its centre is cut from natural yellow-green glass scattered across the Sahara. Ancient Egyptian jewellers were carving genuine impact glass, not shaping paint or dye.

How long before Tutankhamun's reign a rock-shattering impact melted Saharan sand into the glass his jeweller later carved.

It might have been an explosion in the air, not on the ground. A 100-megaton airburst, 200 times the 2013 Chelyabinsk event, could melt sand without leaving a crater. The debate ran for years.

A mineral that only forms from a real ground impact. Reidite, found in roughly one in ten zircon grains across every sample tested, needs shock pressure an airburst cannot produce.

No crater has been found. The glass proves the strike happened anyway.

Sources:
- https://theconversation.com/how-we-solved-the-mystery-of-libyan-desert-glass-117253: written by the Curtin University research team who published the study in the journal Geology, read in full. Establishes that Libyan desert glass formed about 29 million years ago from silica melted above 1,600 degrees Celsius; that the leading rival explanation was a 100-megaton airburst, 200 times the 2013 Chelyabinsk event; and that the discovery of former reidite, a high-pressure mineral, in around 10 per cent of zircon grains across all seven samples studied, is possible only from the shock wave of a genuine meteorite impact, not an airburst, because a 100-megaton airburst of that scale should recur roughly every 10,000 years and the geological record does not support that frequency.
- https://www.ancient-origins.net/artifacts-other-artifacts/tutankhamun-s-scarab-brooch-was-born-28-million-year-old-comet-strike-021509: read in full. Confirms the scarab at the centre of Tutankhamun's brooch is carved from this natural desert glass, and covers a separate 2013 finding by Professor Jan Kramers of the University of Johannesburg: a diamond-bearing pebble found in the same desert, nicknamed 'Hypatia', whose diamonds needed extreme shock pressure to form, proposed as possibly the first known fragment of a comet nucleus found on Earth.
- https://www.britannica.com/biography/Tutankhamun: read in full. Confirms Tutankhamun's reign as king of Egypt from about 1333 BC to 1323 BC, and that his tomb was discovered in the Valley of the Kings in 1922.
